Subject: Hosted API - rate card + quick billing note

Hi J.,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. As promised, attached is our latest Hosted API rate card (Redwood_RateCard_v3.pdf). A couple of quick clarifications up front that came up in the call — I wanted to put them in writing so your procurement and engineering teams have a clear mapping: 

- Billing units: our hosted API charges by tokens (input + output). For both Chat Completions and the newer Responses endpoint we charge on total tokens processed (prompt/context tokens + model-generated tokens). Legacy 'completions' endpoints are also token-billed but may map to older SKU names on invoices.
- Endpoint differences (practical impact): Responses is our newer unified API for streaming + structured outputs and supports function/tool calling; it does not have a separate hidden per-request surcharge — you are billed by tokens. However, because Responses encourages shorter, structured outputs in many flows, customers sometimes see lower effective cost per interaction if they constrain response length.
- Example: 1,000 prompt/context tokens + 2,000 model/output tokens = 3,000 tokens billed. At $X per 1k tokens (baseline on the attached rate card), that’s 3 * $X.

If NeonRetail would consider a committed monthly token volume (we can do a 6/12 month commit), we can provide a volume discount and a simplified monthly invoice that lists committed vs overage. What number would you expect for a production pilot (monthly)?

Next steps: I can loop in finance for formal discount language and CS for a short pilot plan / MIP (mutual implementation plan).

Thanks,
Rafael

Subject: Fwd: Hosted API - rate card + quick billing note (NeonRetail questions)

Folks — forwarding NeonRetail’s follow-ups. They need succinct answers on: token accounting for function calls/streaming, invoice line items (per-endpoint vs aggregated), and a PO template. They are open to a commit/discount.

My proposed quick answers to validate: 
- Token accounting: function/tool calls are part of the model input/output lifecycle — any tokens emitted by the model (including tool call payloads) count toward output tokens. The request payload (prompt + context + tool call args) is counted as input tokens. Aggregate billing = input + output tokens.
- Invoice: we present a single token aggregate line (total tokens) per billing period; we can include a supplemental breakout by endpoint in the invoice details for visibility but it’s not separate pricing SKUs.
- PO fields needed: customer legal name, billing address, PO number, committed monthly tokens (if any), term (months), billing frequency, and contact for invoicing.

For discounting: they asked informally about a volume discount. I propose we offer 18–22% on list rate for a 12-month commit at ~2B tokens/month (pilot → production). Can finance confirm whether 20% flat on hosted baseline is feasible to offer in a signed SOW, and whether we need legal approval for a custom clause?

Also looping CS for a pilot MIP to show expected token profiles (prompt/response averages).

Thanks — Rafael
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API - rate card + quick billing note (NeonRetail questions)

Rafael —

Confirmed high-level answers (happy for you to share directly with NeonRetail):

1) Token accounting (concise customer-friendly wording): Both Chat Completions and Responses are billed on total tokens consumed in a billing period — that is input tokens (prompt + context + any tool-call arguments) plus output tokens (model-generated tokens). Function/tool calls do not add an extra separate line item; any tokens returned by the model when performing a tool call are included in output tokens.

2) Invoice format: invoice will show a single aggregate line for total tokens billed (e.g., 3,000,000 tokens) and the unit price we agreed for the billing tier. We can attach an optional breakdown by endpoint for clarity (CSV), but pricing is applied to the token total.

3) PO template fields: legal entity, billing address, PO number, committed monthly tokens, term length, requested start date, and invoice contact — that’s standard.

4) Discounting: finance can approve a 20% discount off list for a 12-month committed volume with the following guardrails: a minimum commit of 1.5B tokens/month and a 60-day pilot at list pricing (credits applied post-pilot towards commit). Any custom SLA or extended refund terms will need legal review. Laura recommends offering the 20% in the SOW and using a simple table showing committed tokens, effective per-1k price, and overage policy.

Suggested short example to send NeonRetail (include numbers):
- Baseline list price: $0.050 per 1k tokens (Chat/Responses/legacy token measure).
- Example session: 1,000 prompt tokens + 2,000 response tokens = 3,000 tokens billed → 3 * ($0.050 / 1k) = $0.15 (i.e., $0.05 per 1k tokens scaled).
- With a 20% commit discount: effective = $0.040 per 1k tokens. Same token math above applies.

If that looks good I’ll get finance to sign off on formal SOW language and Marissa can draft a short MIP for the pilot.

— Laura
Director, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference

J.,

Thanks for the great questions — below is a compact mapping you can share with procurement/infra. Laura from finance and Marissa from CS are looped for any follow-up.

Short answer (customer-ready): 
- Billing unit: total tokens (input + output). This applies to Chat Completions, Responses, and legacy completions endpoints. Function/tool calls are accounted for as part of input/output tokens — there is no additional per-call charge.
- Invoice: we report a single total-token line item; we can optionally include an endpoint-level CSV for visibility but it does not change pricing.

Concrete example (numbers): 
- Session: 1,000 context/prompt tokens + 2,000 model-output tokens = 3,000 tokens billed.
- Baseline list price (example shown on attached rate card): $0.050 per 1k tokens.
- Cost for this session at list price = (3,000 / 1,000) * $0.050 = $0.15.

Commercial offer: We can provide a 12-month committed plan at 20% off list (effective $0.040 per 1k tokens) with a minimum commitment of 1.5B tokens/month. To mitigate ops risk we typically run a 60-day pilot at list pricing and apply credits toward the first invoice once the SOW is signed. If NeonRetail is comfortable with the guardrails above, I can circulate a short SOW + PO template and a DocuSign link for signatures.
